data: Use these task-oriented guides to install ziprs, create archives, inspect entries, and decompress data. All examples use the same public imports available to downstream Pixi projects.
ziprs works as an ordinary Mojo package while Pixi builds and installs its Rust shared library.
data.install-from-git#Install from Git:
Enable Pixi source builds once, then add the package:
pixi workspace preview add pixi-build pixi add --git "https://github.com/ExtraMojo/zipprs-llm.git" ziprs && pixi install For reproducible builds, replace the branch selected by pixi add with a full rev in pixi.toml.
data.round-trip-in-memory#Round trip in memor:
This example writes one Deflate-compressed file, opens the resulting archive, and decodes the file again without touching the filesystem.
from std.collections import Span from ziprs import Archive, Compression_Deflated, ZipWriter var writer = ZipWriter() var message = String("hello from Mojo") writer.add_file("hello.txt", message.as_bytes(), Compression_Deflated) var encoded = writer.finish() var archive_data = encoded.to_list() var archive = Archive(Span(archive_data)) var index = archive.index_for_name("hello.txt").value() var decoded = archive.read_entry(index).to_list() var text = String(from_utf8=Span(decoded)) print(text) # hello from Mojo Archive owns a copy of archive_data. encoded and decoded are ZipBytes values backed by native storage; to_list() makes Mojo-owned copies when needed.

data:
Archive reads from an in-memory span and keeps its own copy. Look entries up by exact name or iterate their zero-based indexes.
The hidden setup used to test the examples on this page creates a small archive in memory.
from std.collections import Span from ziprs import Archive
data.inspect-metadata-safely#Inspect metadata:
entry() returns a snapshot containing names, sizes, CRC-32, compression information, file kind, and an optional Unix mode.
var metadata = archive.entry(index) print("name:", metadata.name()) print("size:", metadata.size()) print("compressed size:", metadata.compressed_size()) print("compression:", metadata.compression_name()) var safe_name = metadata.enclosed_name() if safe_name: print("safe relative path:", safe_name.value()) else: print("do not extract this entry name") Never join name() directly to an extraction directory. Use enclosed_name() and reject None to block absolute paths, parent traversal, and other unsafe path components. ziprs deliberately does not extract files itself.
data.open-and-find-an-entry#Open and find an: var archive = Archive(Span(source_data)) print("entry count:", archive.len()) var maybe_index = archive.index_for_name("docs/readme.txt") if not maybe_index: raise Error("required entry is missing") var index = maybe_index.value() Names are exact and case-sensitive. A missing name returns None; opening invalid ZIP bytes or using an out-of-range numeric index raises an error.
data.read-an-allocated-result#Read an allocat: var contents = archive.read_entry(index).to_list() var text = String(from_utf8=Span(contents)) print(text) read_entry() allocates storage for the entire uncompressed entry. ZIP data can claim very large uncompressed sizes, so applications should inspect metadata.size() and apply their own limits before reading untrusted archives.
data.read-into-an-exact-size-buffer#Read into:
Use read_into() to control the allocation. The destination length must exactly match the uncompressed entry size; partial reads are rejected.
var destination = List[UInt8](unsafe_uninit_length=Int(metadata.size())) var written = archive.read_into(index, Span(destination)) The archive-level comment is available as raw bytes through archive.comment(). ZIP comments are not guaranteed to be UTF-8, so decode them only when the archive’s encoding is known.

data: ZipWriter accumulates a ZIP archive in memory. Add directory and file entries, optionally attach an archive comment, and call finish() once to write the central directory.
data.build-an-archive#Build an archive: from ziprs import Compression_Deflated, Compression_Stored, ZipWriter var writer = ZipWriter() writer.add_directory("docs/") writer.add_file( "docs/readme.txt", "Compressed text belongs here.\n".as_bytes(), Compression_Deflated, ) writer.add_file( "version.txt", "1\n".as_bytes(), Compression_Stored, ) writer.set_comment("created by ziprs") var encoded = writer.finish() var archive_data = encoded.to_list()
data.choose-compression#Choose compression: Constant Behavior Typical use Compression_Deflated Compresses with Deflate and is the default. Text and other compressible data. Compression_Stored Copies bytes without compression. Already-compressed data or minimum CPU work. Compression is selected per file. Directory entries are Stored automatically.
data.save-the-result#Save the result:
finish() returns ZipBytes. Convert it to a list and pass a span to Mojo’s file API:
from std.collections import Span var archive_data = encoded.to_list() with open("example.zip", "w") as output: output.write_bytes(Span(archive_data)) After finish() succeeds, is_finished() returns True; further calls that add entries, change the comment, or finish again raise an error.

data.modules#Modules: lib: Provides the public in-memory ZIP archive API.
data.ziprs#\u003ccode\u003eziprs\u003c/code\u:
Mojo package 🡭
ziprsReads and writes ZIP archives through a Rust-backed in-memory API.
The package exports Archive for inspection and decompression, ZipWriter for archive creation, Entry for metadata, and ZipBytes for owned native byte buffers. Supported writing methods are Compression_Stored and Compression_Deflated.
Examples:
from std.collections import Span from ziprs import Archive, ZipWriter var writer = ZipWriter() writer.add_file("hello.txt", "hello".as_bytes()) var archive_bytes = writer.finish() var encoded = archive_bytes.to_list() var archive = Archive(Span(encoded)) var index = archive.index_for_name("hello.txt").value() var decoded = archive.read_entry(index).to_list() print(String(from_utf8=Span(decoded)))

data.lib#\u003ccode\u003elib\u003c/code\u003e:
Mojo module 🡭
libProvides the public in-memory ZIP archive API.
The structs in this module own their Rust-backed resources. Archive input bytes are copied when an Archive is opened, and ZipWriter produces an owned ZipBytes buffer when finished.
Examples:
from std.collections import Span from ziprs import Archive, Compression_Deflated, ZipWriter var writer = ZipWriter() var message = String("hello from Mojo") writer.add_file("hello.txt", message.as_bytes(), Compression_Deflated) var encoded = writer.finish() var archive_data = encoded.to_list() var archive = Archive(Span(archive_data)) var index = archive.index_for_name("hello.txt").value() var decoded = archive.read_entry(index).to_list() print(String(from_utf8=Span(decoded)))
data.structs#Structs: ZipBytes: Owns a byte buffer returned by the Rust ZIP implementation. Archive: Reads entry metadata and contents from an in-memory ZIP archive. ZipWriter: Builds a ZIP archive entirely in memory.

data.archive#\u003ccode\u003eArchive\u003c/co:
Mojo struct 🡭
Archive @memory_only struct Archive Reads entry metadata and contents from an in-memory ZIP archive.
Opening an archive copies the input span into native-owned storage, so the caller may release or reuse the original bytes afterward. Entry indexes are zero-based and remain valid for the lifetime of the archive.
Examples:
var archive = Archive(Span(archive_data)) print("entries:", archive.len()) for raw_index in range(Int(archive.len())): var entry = archive.entry(UInt(raw_index)) print(entry.name(), entry.size())
data.methods#Methods:
➕  ➖ __init__ def __init__(out self, data: Span[UInt8]) Opens a ZIP archive from an in-memory byte span. Args:
data (Span[UInt8]): The complete encoded ZIP archive. The bytes are copied. self (Self) Returns:
Self
Raises:
An error if the data is not a valid or supported ZIP archive.
open @staticmethod def open(data: Span[UInt8]) -> Self Opens a ZIP archive from an in-memory byte span. This named constructor is equivalent to Archive(data).
Args:
data (Span[UInt8]): The complete encoded ZIP archive. The bytes are copied. Returns:
Self: The opened archive.
Raises:
An error if the data is not a valid or supported ZIP archive.
len def len(self) -> UInt Returns the number of entries in the archive. Args:
self (Self) Returns:
UInt: The number of file and directory entries.
Raises:
An error if the underlying native archive is no longer valid.
is_empty def is_empty(self) -> Bool Checks whether the archive contains no entries. Args:
self (Self) Returns:
Bool: True when Archive.len is zero, otherwise False.
Raises:
An error if the underlying native archive is no longer valid.
index_for_name def index_for_name(self, name: String) -> Optional[UInt] Looks up an entry index by its exact stored name. Names are case-sensitive and use the separators stored in the archive.
Examples:
var maybe_index = archive.index_for_name("docs/readme.txt") if maybe_index: print("entry index:", maybe_index.value()) Args:
self (Self) name (String): The exact entry name to find. Returns:
Optional[UInt]: The zero-based index when present, otherwise None.
Raises:
An error if the underlying native archive is no longer valid.
entry def entry(mut self, index: UInt) -> Entry Returns an immutable metadata snapshot for one entry. Args:
self (Self) index (UInt): A zero-based index smaller than Archive.len. Returns:
Entry: Metadata including the name, sizes, CRC-32, compression method, file kind, and optional Unix mode.
Raises:
An error if the index is out of range or the native archive is invalid.
read_entry def read_entry(mut self, index: UInt) -> ZipBytes Decompresses an entry into a newly allocated byte buffer. Directory entries normally produce an empty buffer. For caller-provided storage, use Archive.read_into instead.
Examples:
var index = archive.index_for_name("hello.txt").value() var bytes = archive.read_entry(index).to_list() print(String(from_utf8=Span(bytes))) Args:
self (Self) index (UInt): A zero-based index smaller than Archive.len. Returns:
ZipBytes: The complete uncompressed entry contents.
Raises:
An error if the index is out of range, the entry cannot be decompressed, memory cannot be reserved, or the native archive is invalid.
read_into def read_into(mut self, index: UInt, buffer: Span[UInt8]) -> UInt Decompresses an entry into an exact-size caller-provided buffer. The destination length must equal Entry.size() for the selected entry. No partial reads are performed.
Examples:
var entry = archive.entry(index) var destination = List[UInt8](unsafe_uninit_length=Int(entry.size())) var written = archive.read_into(index, Span(destination)) Args:
self (Self) index (UInt): A zero-based index smaller than Archive.len. buffer (Span[UInt8]): A mutable destination whose length exactly matches the uncompressed entry size. Returns:
UInt: The number of bytes written, equal to len(buffer) on success.
Raises:
An error if the index is invalid, the destination has the wrong length, decompression fails, or the native archive is invalid.
comment def comment(self) -> ZipBytes Returns the archive-level comment as raw bytes. ZIP comments are not required to be UTF-8. Convert the returned bytes to String only when the archive’s encoding is known.
Args:
self (Self) Returns:
ZipBytes: The archive comment, or an empty buffer when no comment is present.
Raises:
An error if the underlying native archive is no longer valid.

➕  ➖ len def len(self) -> UInt Returns the number of bytes in the buffer. Args:
self (Self) Returns:
UInt: The buffer length in bytes.
Raises:
An error if the underlying native value is no longer valid.
fill def fill(self, buffer: Span[UInt8]) -> UInt Copies bytes into an existing mutable span. At most len(buffer) bytes are copied. Use a destination of ZipBytes.len bytes to copy the entire value.
Examples:
var destination = List[UInt8](unsafe_uninit_length=Int(contents.len())) var copied = contents.fill(Span(destination)) Args:
self (Self) buffer (Span[UInt8]): The destination span to fill. Returns:
UInt: The number of bytes copied.
Raises:
An error if the underlying native value is no longer valid.
to_list def to_list(self) -> List[UInt8] Copies the complete buffer into a new Mojo List[UInt8]. Examples:
var bytes = contents.to_list() var text = String(from_utf8=Span(bytes)) Args:
self (Self) Returns:
List[UInt8]: A newly allocated list containing every byte.
Raises:
An error if the native value is invalid or the native copy reports an unexpected length.
data.zipbytes#\u003ccode\u003eZipBytes\u003c/:
Mojo struct 🡭
ZipBytes @memory_only struct ZipBytes Owns a byte buffer returned by the Rust ZIP implementation.
ZipBytes values contain either a completed archive from ZipWriter.finish, entry contents from Archive.read_entry, or an archive comment from Archive.comment. Copy the bytes into Mojo-owned storage with ZipBytes.to_list or into an existing destination with ZipBytes.fill.

data.methods#Methods:
➕  ➖ __init__ def __init__(out self) Creates an empty in-memory ZIP writer. Args:
self (Self) Returns:
Self
Raises:
An error if the native writer cannot be initialized.
is_finished def is_finished(self) -> Bool Checks whether ZipWriter.finish has already consumed the writer output. Args:
self (Self) Returns:
Bool: True after a successful call to ZipWriter.finish, otherwise False.
Raises:
An error if the underlying native writer is no longer valid.
add_file def add_file(mut self, name: String, data: Span[UInt8], compression: Int32 = Int32(1)) Adds one file entry and copies its data into the archive. Examples:
var payload = String("important data") writer.add_file("data.txt", payload.as_bytes(), Compression_Stored) Args:
self (Self) name (String): The path stored in the ZIP directory, conventionally using / separators. data (Span[UInt8]): The uncompressed file contents. compression (Int32): Compression_Deflated by default, or Compression_Stored. Raises:
An error if the writer is finished, the compression value is unsupported, or the entry cannot be written.
add_directory def add_directory(mut self, name: String) Adds an explicit directory entry. Examples:
writer.add_directory("images/") Args:
self (Self) name (String): The directory path to store. A trailing / is recommended. Raises:
An error if the writer is finished or the directory entry cannot be written.
set_comment def set_comment(mut self, comment: String) Sets the archive-level UTF-8 comment. Calling this method again replaces the previous comment.
Args:
self (Self) comment (String): The comment text to store. Raises:
An error if the writer is finished or the comment cannot be stored.
finish def finish(mut self) -> ZipBytes Finalizes the central directory and returns the encoded archive. This method succeeds only once. Use ZipWriter.is_finished to query the writer state.
Examples:
var archive_bytes = writer.finish() var storage = archive_bytes.to_list() with open("example.zip", "w") as output: output.write_bytes(Span(storage)) Args:
self (Self) Returns:
ZipBytes: The complete encoded ZIP archive.
Raises:
An error if the writer was already finished or finalization fails.
data.zipwriter#\u003ccode\u003eZipWriter\u003:
Mojo struct 🡭
ZipWriter @memory_only struct ZipWriter Builds a ZIP archive entirely in memory.
Add files and directories, optionally set an archive comment, then call ZipWriter.finish exactly once. Stored and Deflate compression are supported. A finished writer rejects further mutations.
Examples:
var writer = ZipWriter() writer.add_directory("docs/") writer.add_file( "docs/hello.txt", "hello from Mojo".as_bytes(), Compression_Deflated, ) writer.set_comment("created by ziprs") var archive_bytes = writer.finish()
